Jakyeong gasped, snapping his head forward only to meet Il-hyun’s vicious glare.

Woof! Woof!

A German Shepherd was bounding across the lawn, pursued by a frantic guard who hauled the dog toward the rear courtyard. In that fleeting second, the guard’s eyes drifted upward toward the window—only for him to instantly avert his gaze and sprint away in sheer panic.

Jakyeong’s soul left his body. The guards had seen everything. As if Wang Han catching them weren't mortifying enough, now the entire security detail knew.

“Stop pouting. There isn’t a single soul in this compound who doesn't know we’re fucking.”

Asshole. Jakyeong glared daggers, but Il-hyun abruptly drove all the way in with devastating force. The broad head slammed squarely into his prostate, sending electric shocks shivering down to his toes. Ah—! Squeezing his eyes shut, Jakyeong blindly reached out, and Il-hyun willingly offered his throat.

Still impaled, Jakyeong latched onto his neck. Thwack, thwack, thwack. The pounding turned so savage that Jakyeong’s body was folded and crushed against him, blinding white sparks exploding behind his eyelids. His mind wiped clean of all shame; he no longer gave a single damn who was watching. Desperately seeking anchor, he smashed his lips onto Il-hyun’s, kissing him with frantic hunger.

Peeking through half-lidded eyes, he saw the corner of Il-hyun’s mouth curve into a dark smirk. Thud, thud. The hips slammed with bruising momentum until, with a sharp swell in Jakyeong’s gut, a scalding flood erupted deep inside him.

They remained locked together, exchanging soft, lingering kisses as the aftershocks subsided. When they finally parted for air, Il-hyun gently smoothed the sweat-drenched bangs from Jakyeong’s forehead.

“Looks like I’ll have to be celibate for a whole month.”

He chuckled, but Jakyeong couldn't even manage a smirk. He’s really sending me away. Not long ago, escaping to some island had been his absolute dream. He should have been jumping for joy, yet an inexplicable pit of heavy, suffocating anxiety sat in his chest.

Human hearts were truly impossible to decipher.

"How long are you going to stay buried under there?"

Despite Wang Han’s exasperated scolding, Wang Ryun remained curled beneath the hospital blanket, utterly motionless.

After raging like a rabid beast yesterday, he had completely shut down today, lying limp like a corpse. Jakyeong had tried coaxing him out with dry jokes, but the man was entirely unresponsive.

Even the news of a month-long luxury stay in an oceanfront Hawaiian villa failed to elicit a twitch. For a man who lived for tropical beaches and luxury resorts, the silence proved just how deeply the betrayal had shattered him.

Letting out a heavy sigh, Jakyeong followed Han out of the VIP ward after a few more futile attempts at comfort.

The plan was for the two of them to return to the estate first and pack the luggage.

The sky had been bruising into an ominous, purplish black all morning, and the moment they stepped through the glass doors, a torrential wall of rain slammed down on the asphalt. Slipping into the driver's seat, Jakyeong turned the ignition and ran a hand through his damp hair.

He flicked the wipers to maximum, but the downpour was so dense the windshield remained a blurred sheet of water. Deciding holding out was pointless, he put the sedan into gear, and Il-hyun’s surveillance detail pulled out of the opposite lot to trail them.

Navigating through the city, traffic crawled beneath the deluge.

"Will Ryun-ge stay like this forever?" Jakyeong asked, eyes on the road.

"Who knows. I just hope he snaps out of it soon."

"Should I track her down?"

With their underworld connections, cornering Yoon Mi-ra wouldn't take more than a few days. Yet finding her would fix nothing—the betrayal was etched in stone, and rebuilding broken trust between operatives was an impossible fantasy.

The signal ahead turned red, and the car rolled to a halt.

Jakyeong checked the rearview mirror. The trailing security sedan was missing from behind.

Glancing sideways, he spotted the vehicle idling directly parallel to their flank. Keeping pace side-by-side was an unusual tactical formation for Il-hyun's tail.

The light flicked green. Jakyeong accelerated, turning right onto a newly paved arterial bypass. With the weekday weather so foul, the multi-lane road was completely barren of civilian traffic.

As they picked up speed, the adjacent car began aggressively crowding their lane, matching their speed bumper-to-bumper.

The erratic maneuvering set Jakyeong’s teeth on edge. Han noticed the anomaly as well, cracking his window to look across.

What's their problem? Did something happen?

The driver's window of the adjacent vehicle glided down smoothly.

Instead of the standard black wool suit worn by Il-hyun's detail, the driver was clad in a casual gray jacket.

Jakyeong leaned in to look—and his breath instantly froze in his throat. Beside him, Wang Han locked into total, paralyzed shock.

Sitting behind the wheel, staring back with cold, dead eyes while leveling a suppressed automatic pistol directly at their heads, was Takeya Jun.

The old instructor who had allegedly arrived in Korea yesterday to "take care of business."

SLAM!

Jakyeong floored the throttle, the engine roaring as the car lurched forward.

CRACK.

A heavy 9mm slug shattered the rear quarter-glass, spraying tempered shards across the backseat.

A millisecond's hesitation would have left both of their skulls ventilated.

Jakyeong gripped the steering wheel with white knuckles, checking the mirror. Jun’s sedan surged forward with terrifying velocity, ramming their rear bumper with a concussive BANG.

The impact threw both men forward against their seatbelts. Jakyeong fought the wheel, his jaw clenching hard.

"What the fuck is that bastard doing here?!"

Han’s face went paper-white as the pieces violently clicked together in his head. The contract Jun mentioned... was it on us?

Fuck. We walked right into the crosshairs.

Jun’s vehicle surged forward again, slamming hard into their driver's side door. Metal screamed against metal, the impact forcing their chassis dangerously close to the concrete guardrail.

"Get the guns!" Jakyeong roared.

Han scrambled, tearing through the glove compartment and reaching beneath the passenger seat, his expression instantly dropping into horror.

"Ah... shit!"

They had sent the sedan for an extensive interior detailing three days ago, stripping every hidden firearm from the cabin. With no active threats on their radar, they hadn't reloaded the cache.

"Goddamn it!" Han yelled, slamming his fist into the dash.

BANG! BANG!

A volley of gunfire erupted through the downpour.

Their side mirror sheared off in an explosion of plastic, and the front passenger glass shattered into a thousand jagged teeth.

Jakyeong ground his teeth until they ached, swerving violently across the slick asphalt to break the angle, yet Jun’s sedan shadowed every drift with lethal, mechanical precision.
